title: The Easter Vigil readings
hookLine: up to seven readings, from creation to Ezekiel, before the alleluia
carry: the whole story in one night

cards: It's dark outside, and the church is dark inside. A fire is lit at the door. A single tall candle is carried in, and the flame passes hand to hand down the pews until the whole room is lit by small candles.
A deacon or cantor sings the Exsultet, the great Easter proclamation. Then everyone sits down, because this is going to take a while.
Before anyone says alleluia, the Church opens the Bible at page one and reads its way forward.

teach.b: The Missal gives seven readings from the Old Testament, each followed by a psalm and a prayer. It starts with creation, in the Douay-Rheims: "In the beginning God created heaven, and earth."
And soon: "Be light made. And light was made." In that church, the candle that just came in the door was the first light, too. Then Abraham on the mountain with Isaac.
Then the sea parting at the Exodus, the one reading the Missal says may never be left out, because that crossing from slavery to freedom is the pattern for Easter.

teach.h: A HEART OF STONE, A HEART OF FLESH.
teach.b: Then the prophets: Isaiah promising a love that won't leave, and water and bread for anyone who's thirsty; Baruch praising wisdom; and last, Ezekiel, where God promises to take away the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh.
Parishes may shorten the list, but the Missal asks for at least three, and the Red Sea always stays.

teach.h: THEN THE BELLS, THEN THE ALLELUIA.
teach.b: Then the candles on the altar are lit, the bells ring out for the Gloria, and the reading from Romans says that in baptism we are buried with Christ and rise with him.
Only then does the alleluia return, sung for the first time since Lent began. Why read the whole story? Because the Church's claim is that Easter isn't a lucky ending tacked on.

teach.h: BE LIGHT MADE. AND LIGHT WAS MADE.
teach.b: It's what the whole story was heading toward, from the first light. Adults preparing for baptism are baptized at this Mass, after the readings and the homily.
They hear the family history on the night they join the family.

how: At the Easter Vigil, Catholics gather after dark, light the Easter candle from a new fire, hear up to seven Old Testament readings with psalms, then sing the Gloria and the first alleluia since Lent; adults preparing for baptism are baptized and confirmed at this Mass.

games.q: you're the pastor, and the Vigil is running long. you can cut readings. which one does the Missal say you must keep?
o: the crossing of the Red Sea from Exodus.
games.why: the Exodus reading is never omitted. the crossing from slavery to freedom is the pattern the Church reads Easter through.

practice: Open a Bible or an app to Genesis 1 and read slowly, as if you were in that dark church with a candle in your hand; you don't have to finish.
Notice the rhythm, God said, and it was made, and it was good, then close it and think of the first light you saw this morning. If you pray, you can thank God for one thing that was made.

wordCard.voice: Exsultet, let it rejoice. The great Easter proclamation sung by candlelight before the Vigil's readings begin, from the first light to Ezekiel's heart of flesh. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: let it rejoice, the first word of the Easter proclamation sung before the readings.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole story in one night. From the first light to a heart of flesh. Tomorrow, the alleluia.
